227.name: Footstep of Gods
227.lore: A group of Kephale followers were obsessed with finding giant footprints. They claimed those are the proofs of Kephale once walking on earth, and people would receive the Titan's blessing if they stood in the footprints. Another group smelled a business opportunity from this rumor. They were dedicated to finding new footprints, then building exhibition halls around the prints and charging a fee for pilgrims coming to worship. These activities drew a third kind of people, the craftsmen and businesses that sold miniature models of the footprint around the halls. Maybe boosting commerce is also a form of Kephale's blessing.

228.name: Memory of Stars
228.lore: The beaches to the west of Amphoreus are different to all other beaches — They are ashen black. The followers of Oronyx would go there to pick sea conchs during low tide, claiming that everyone was a star in the sky before they were born and that upon the person's death, their star would fall into the River of Souls, which then washes the star into the sea and forms conchs. They, therefore, believe that sea conchs contain the voices and memories of the dead, and the conchs can answer when spoken to. This myth became more and more fantastical over the years, culminating in the belief that sea conchs have the power of prophecy. People therefore asked the conchs countless questions and, when no satisfactory answer was received, would cook the conchs and serve them up as a dish.

229.name: Simple Judgment
229.lore: Talanton's royal judges would only take out the Judgment Device when faced with the most enigmatic cases. The lion heads on the two sides of the device would each tightly clamp down on a piece of evidence — These could be a bloodstained dagger or a bottle of poisoned honey brew, and the scale would always tilt favorably towards the item that's more indicative of the truth. While some culprits can indeed create "perfect crimes," they tend to forget that the most reliable evidence will always remain in their hearts. Put the suspect's finger into the lion's mouth, and Talanton will show them how their denials are nothing before the lions' teeth.

230.name: Self-Amusement
230.lore: Drinking and listening to music are the only two hobbies a Mythemian will have in their lives. Therefore, brewers and musicians are the most respected professions in that entire city. There was once a "person" who simultaneously reached the zenith of both crafts — It was a machine created by the Grand Craftsman Phionisius while in a drunken stupor. The machine once played enchanting melodies while brewing charming wine in a feast held by the king, and drowned all guests present in supreme bliss. However, the story had a tragic end. The king wished to claim the machine and therefore killed the craftsman, while the machine had grown attached to the craftsman and therefore poisoned the king. In the end, the royal guards tore that intricate machine to pieces.

231.name: Sapient Pen
231.lore: A Grove scholar once had so many ideas that the slow speed of writing with human hands made him lose out on many inspired moments. He therefore made a pen from a small branch of Cerces and various valuable gemstones. That pen can write many times faster than an ordinary pen, but it took so long to develop that its maker died soon after its completion. Nonetheless, that invention still found glory in the annals of history — Since the sages love to punish apprentices by making them copy an essay a few hundred times, all Grove apprentices ended up having one copy of this pen each.

232.name: Love-Seeking Golden Dart
232.lore: If you were invited to the group date parties hosted by the most fanatic Mnestia followers, then I recommend that you go not in elegant gowns but in a suit of armor — Or at least go with a helmet. You'll thank me when you're facing the golden darts flying chaotically all over the space. Those followers are of the firm belief that the golden dart can find love for them, and the person it stabs is the true love destined for the one who threw the dart. You know, this manner of courting actually has some sense — If someone can still talk to you peacefully after being stabbed in the head by a dart you threw, then they sure have the potential to become your partner.

233.name: Asat Pramad's Die (Head)
233.lore: Due to his bizarre aesthetics of destruction, Asat Pramad has garnered quite a following in the cosmos. After an acceptable amount of staff casualties, the nosy daredevils from Interastral Peace Entertainment managed to snap photos of this Lord Ravager and produced a set of fan merchandise based on his image. However, due to some as-yet-unknown principle, this die always lands on the same number. The Intelligentsia Guild speculates that this is because randomness, or chaos, is an essential component of Elation. "If a die knew its result before being cast, wouldn't that take all the fun out of it?"

234.name: Darksea Bait Chunks
234.lore: The Astral Ecology School's work on Shattered Star Bait yielded a new substance that had an enticing effect on void song whales and other large creatures. This innovation propelled the advancement of the space whaling industry, accelerating ecological deterioration. According to unreliable sources, the IPC had originally planned to use it to lure Luxbane, until relevant personnel discovered during a large-scale experiment that humans were also attracted to it.

235.name: Sealing Wax of Trailblaze
235.lore: There is a saying amongst the dejected Self-Annihilators that the universe has no purpose and humans are nothing in the eyes of the Aeons. If the Aeons truly stand above all lifeforms and rule supreme, then why would they care about the everyday concerns of mortals? The existence of the sleeping and shapeless IX is proof of that. To show the Self-Annihilators that the Aeons do care, the Doctors of Chaos combined the demon god crafts of the occult monks to create the Sealing Wax of Aeons. It is said that stamping with this Sealing Wax will attract a glimpse from the corresponding Aeon from across space and time — There are no successful examples yet, but some Self-Annihilators did regain their faith in the universe, Aeons, and everything else after stamping with this sealing wax.

236.name: Black Hole Sugar Maker
236.lore: Genius Society 3 Nyul Iman once recreated a black hole in her laboratory, and people speculated she was seeking the essence of Nihility. Three weeks later, she modified the Synthetic Black Hole into a cotton candy machine that automatically dispensed sweets to passing children, which led onlookers to suspect her true study was Voracity. The Fools offered a simpler hypothesis: perhaps she was just curious about what a black hole might taste like. In the end, she made far too much for one person to ever eat alone.

237.name: Transform!!!
237.lore: A watch with transformation function, originally an official merchandise from the *Super Ninja Squad*. In this collaboration with *Cosmic Ninjutsu Inscriptions* where Night Blade warriors would shout bizarre ninjutsu names and transform under the cover of smoke... That was, until a Fool infiltrated the production line and imbued the device with genuine transformation function, turning it into an extremely dangerous item. To this day, all units have been sealed away in storage.

238.name: Featherlight Inscription
238.lore: Planet Nikota has complex and solemn funeral traditions. Residents hold grand ceremonies for the deceased, and the government has laws prohibiting the desecration of tombstones. As time passed, the planet gradually became occupied by tombstones, leaving less and less living space for the living. Masked Fool Urima lived on Nikota for <unbreak>40</unbreak> years, attending thousands of funerals where guests would weep endlessly, with no hint of joy. So he planned a special funeral for himself: in front of everyone, his tombstone sprouted thrusters and soared into the sky to pounding beats, the exhaust flames burning an epitaph into the grass: "Come on, smile! Isn't it vast out there?"

239.name: Glow-Up
239.lore: Once all the rage in Amphoreus, this skincare product worked wonders with a simple spray: a veil of golden powder that smoothed wrinkles, brightened, and moisturized the skin. Rumors claimed its essence was drawn from the summit of the Hero's Bath, retrievable only by Chrysos Heir heroes. But as the bath's proprietress grew in divinity, such skincare products vanished completely from the market.

240.name: Telepathic Fork
240.lore: Some radical members of the Universal Culinary Society believe that eating and hunger are the Primum Mobile of the Path of Voracity, but consuming food prepared by others is heresy. Insisting on personally completing the entire process from slaughter to cooking and tenderizing meat through life-or-death combat, they forged these "thermal weapons," which was meant for heating. The outcome, however, often ends up with ingredients being blasted into charcoal.

241.name: Sage's Leaf Robe
241.lore: "A Sage must wear a beard!" No one knows which Sage from the Grove of Epiphany first proposed this idea, but it quickly gained enthusiastic support. Soon, Sages were adorning their sparse chins with gathered twigs and leaves. That meeting of the Sages ended in joyous laughter, and the robes made from branches and leaves became their official attire. It is said that under Cerces's witness, these robes would sprout new leaves as wisdom grows, just like a beard would.

242.name: Green Miracle
242.lore: Argas lies to the south of Dolos, a land perpetually tormented by drought, where sand dominates the terrain. A compassionate traveler passing through decided to seek plants from Cerces that could transform the desert. After enduring countless hardships, he finally obtained a blessed seed from Cerces, yet it perished in the dust before it could ever sprout. In his moment of despair, the traveler discovered that he himself was the one truly blessed. And so, he sowed himself into the earth. They say that to this day, he's still growing in the oasis.

243.name: Express Fragment Memorial Plaque
243.lore: A legend circulates in the city of Okhema: a falling star descended into the Abyss of Fate, bringing with it a Deliverer from beyond the sky. The priests and treasure hunters searched the area, finding meteorite fragments scattered everywhere. They collected these pieces to craft talismans, believing that one day they would help people break free from the shackles of destiny. Some say this story was fabricated by Zagreus's followers: how could a celestial meteor be so easily refined? Yet even if the material of these pendants isn't genuine, the spirit dwelling within them holds real power.

244.name: Minotaur Hunt
244.lore: A set of treasure maps that dynamically track monsters. In the labyrinthine hunting grounds of Planet Minotaur, hunting Minotaurs was once an incredibly popular activity. However, as Minotaurs faced extinction due to environmental degradation, the activity was forcibly suspended two Amber Eras ago. Nevertheless, conservation specialists from the Intelligentsia Guild have implanted tracking chips in every surviving Minotaur and developed a rather reliable population recovery plan. Perhaps in the near future, people will once again be able to shout that classic hunter line in the maze: "Holy cow, there's a bull!"

245.name: Supreme Glue
245.lore: When the Golden Banana Planet split into several pieces due to a forbidden experiment, Dr. Primitive merely chuckled and pulled out the Supreme Glue from his pocket, sticking the planetary fragments back together. No one knew why Dr. Primitive initially invented this overpowered adhesive until one day, while evading Rangers' pursuit, he deliberately scattered some mass-produced Supreme Glue across the universe for passing merchant ships to collect. This genius creation that could "fix anything" instantly caused an uproar across the cosmos. Some used it to build houses, while others installed bombs. One even tried to mend a broken relationship, and when that failed, they settled for gluing themself to their partner, never to part again.

246.name: Eye of Overseer
246.lore: During Cerydra's reign, faith in Talanton flourished like never before. Many people took it upon themselves to crack down on law violations, begging Talanton to pass judgment on all sorts of trivial matters, but the Scale of Justice rarely responded. It was then that the "Eye of Overseer" came into being. It could record sights and sounds to help courts reach verdicts, and could only be used by true believers of Talanton. Before the Flame-Chase Journey began, all Eyes of Overseer were destroyed, as too many people discovered they weren't true believers of Talanton after all.

247.name: Encouragement for You
247.lore: As a History Fictionologist, Thym places great emphasis on education through positive reinforcement, which might be related to his not-so-pleasant childhood. To comfort disheartened children, he designed a unique "encouragement" vessel. Whenever a child receives praise, the power of encouragement materializes in front of them as flame, shaped as a thumbs-up. The more encouragement received, the brighter the flame burns. However, when he tried to promote this idea across the universe, he faced opposition from many parents. Because children shouldn't play with fire.

248.name: Frozen Virtue
248.lore: Hundreds of Amber Eras ago, the Kolchis considered devouring others as a sign of great respect. When a baby was born, the entire Kalsasian community would mobilize to care for it. And for their deceased members, the Lapispeakers would craft a special information flake as a burial offering... These beautiful virtues are gradually disappearing with the progression of time. The pessimists of the Garden of Recollection proposed that universal morality should be preserved through emergency measures. However, which virtues are truly worth preserving still seems to be up for debate.

249.name: Winterfish Summerherb
249.lore: Poets rarely associate Cerces with Phagousa, with the Winterfish Summerherb being one of the exceptions. In extremely rare cases, a fish that should dwell in the sea would leap onto the riverbank, swallow a seed from the Mori tree, and return alive to the water. This seed would then, by pure chance, sprout inside a fish's belly and be caught by fishermen, with odds even lower than rolling four sixes in a row. That's why sailors use the phrase "catching a Winterfish Summerherb" to describe nearly impossible events. Still, many insisted such a rarity must be a potent tonic. King Theseus, on his deathbed, had sent for it, only to die of food poisoning after taking it.

250.name: Antimatter Engine Controller
250.lore: During the early attempts to replicate the Astral Express, the Technology Department struggled to solve the engine's power issue. The Intelligentsia Guild proposed using antimatter to replace the power of Trailblaze, with this controller serving as a matching component. The original design concept was simple: just like adjusting the hot and cold water ratio in a shower head, one could control the Express's speed by cleverly adjusting the injection rate of matter and antimatter with a wrench. However, prototype testing always ended in annihilating explosions. After all, getting the water temperature right was never an easy task.

251.name: Absolute Sound Quality
251.lore: The Vannesians are renowned for their extraordinary musical talent, having been ranked among the top five most musically-gifted species in the universe. They communicate through beautiful chords and rejected the invitation from the Harmony Family, solely to pursue the pure beauty of rhythm. However, after receiving the Abundance's blessing, this pursuit began to turn pathological. For instance, in their pursuit of flawless vocal reproduction, the Vannesians used biotechnology to create these biological headsets with living mouths integrated into the earpads, which perform the audio directly, eliminating any timbral distortion.

252.name: Interstellar Roaming Pager
252.lore: As more planets joined the pan-cosmic market, the IPC urgently needed a miniaturized hyper-distant delivery device for employees stationed in frontier regions. Eventually, the School of Pure Creation's "Interstellar Roaming Pager" won the bid. This device inherited the virtues of the Amber Lord: sturdy enough to serve as a noodle-cup weight, can opener, and emergency survival hammer all in one. Its signal was equally tenacious, maintaining a connection anywhere in the cosmos, even from within a black hole. Once deployed, frontier planets promptly saw a significant drop in absenteeism rates.

262.name: Perilous Memory Storage
262.lore: The Memosnatcher Mausolea once issued a heist notice to the Governor of Merlo Sector, threatening to steal and publicize the deepest secrets within his mind. To counter her threat, the governor commissioned the Intelligentsia Guild to develop this storage device. He transferred <unbreak>2,136</unbreak> memory segments marked "High Risk" into it, intending to destroy them with the push of a button when the time came. When the Memosnatcher arrived, the hard drive failed to function as anticipated, since the Governor had long forgotten how to operate it. Ultimately, however, it still repelled the Memosnatcher when thrown directly at her. After all, it is a high-density block of information, which is effectively a brick to a memetic lifeform.

263.name: Flatbread
263.lore: Before the Second Great Prosperity, interstellar travel was an absolute slog. Limited by the technology of the time, ships often took months just to cross a star system, while long-distance voyages were measured in years. Many sailors would end up losing themselves in the boundless cosmos, succumbing to depression or delirium, even treating the control console as their best friend. To assist in crew psychological intervention, a Doctor of Chaos named Pino invented "Positive Emotion Hardtack." Consumers would recall the happiest moments of their lives, enabling them to do anything with a positive attitude. However, after its widespread adoption, many employees used it during performance reviews to derive happiness from working overtime. The IPC quickly banned the production of these hardtacks. Nowadays, people must rely on their own strength to confront the sense of desolate emptiness.

264.name: Terminal Defender
264.lore: The Interastral Entertainment Network brought a trendy new wave of entertainment to Planarcadia, much to the distaste of many Fools at the tavern. By blasting it with trashy short videos and relentless gaslighting every day, a Masked Fool named Empath finally nurtured a "Terminal Guard" plant. Fueled by a hatred for online chaos, every one of its leaves can purify over 1 Tbps of data, automatically blocking objectionable content on terminals. Following the successful experiment, Empath placed these plants in restrooms all over Planarcadia, only to find them swiftly removed by other people, since virtually all internet content was deemed "objectionable" by the Guard. More importantly, with such powerful blocking features, it really didn't look like a plant anymore.

265.name: Armed Archaeological Shovel
265.lore: Armed Archaeologists are truly the oddballs of the Intelligentsia Guild. Many scholars in this faction are obsessed with combining weaponry and excavation tools, just so they can come in handy at critical moments. <unbreak>15</unbreak> Amber Eras ago, an archaeological team from the Sandridge-III Observation Station landed on a planet's surface, intending to study the remains of a Swarm King stranded there. However, a swarm of True Stings buried deep underground suddenly revived during the sampling process. The team suffered heavy casualties, leaving only their leader, Slay, alive. He held out alone on the planet for 5 years, continuing the excavation while fighting off the incoming Swarm with his armed archaeological shovel. Yet, when the IPC fleet arrived for the rescue, Slay resisted violently, eventually choosing to end his own life due to the "unshakable buzzing" in his head.

266.name: Mining Dust Collector
266.lore: Nomadic miners don't always mine deposits — the Terramite-III is a massive airship designed specifically for mining planets, integrating residential, refining, and other functional modules. The giant drill it carries can directly shatter an entire asteroid, with surrounding tractor beams collecting the debris. It is said that a certain miner group violated the *Interastral Security Treaty* by using this ship to strip away an entire continent from the planet Olander. But the locals were more amazed by the thing's appearance than what the planet had lost, since it looked exactly like a vacuum robot from Interastral Peace Appliances, just magnified tens of millions of times. The miners, meanwhile, admit it's one of their most trusted designs.

267.name: Cosmic Drifter Fish
267.lore: In the asteroid belt of Apex Segmentum, there wanders a silicon-based lifeform known as the drifter fish. For the most part, they move by drifting, slow as space junk, and were once ranked in the top five of the "Least Dangerous Intellitrons." That is, until the Second Emperor's War, when people discovered that their fin-like tails actually concealed high-energy thrusters capable of reaching one-tenth the speed of light in just thirty seconds at full power. In the end, the Marketing Development Department paid the price of the entire Third Fleet to "exterminate" the drifter fish. However, in the Solar Sailboat Competition held in <unbreak>2120</unbreak> AE, the IPC representative Hekas Iron-Eye took first place using four drifter fish as propulsion, declaring the domestication of the species complete.

268.name: Vonwacq Souvenir
268.lore: Wacq Island on Vonwacq is one of the most biodiverse places in the universe. Unlike other islands, every creature here has a lethal gimmick. The Six-Toothed Flower is the weakest plant of the lot, as its teeth are only as hard as diamonds, and it hunts far slower than the average animal, nearly causing its extinction. Outsiders arriving on Wacq Island recognized the value of Six-Toothed Flowers and brought them to the Interastral Peace Market. After generations of selective breeding, the plant became both beautiful and safe, sparking a brief wave of hype. It's said its popularity comes from the realization people have while looking at it: In Vonwacq, you're nothing but a seed.

269.name: Wishing Nickel
269.lore: In the Canvas Age, almost everyone could consume Wishpower, and Wishing Nickels were the most accessible medium. Whatever was written on them had a probability of coming true as long as one was pious enough. Initially, people pinned their hopes for a better life on the nickels: Romance, promotions, or just having a good day... But after spending too many years in the Eternal Canvas, the wishes people made grew increasingly distorted, such as sending their neighbors spiraling into the sky or paving the roads with banana peels. The Worlds Reborn Initiative did not salvage these Wishing Nickels, which was why some residents preferred to remain in the painting, continuing their game of mutual wish-making.

270.name: Inspiration Glass Ball
270.lore: A brilliant reversal, a meticulous deduction, a novel framework... All those elusive flashes of inspiration across every field vanish in an instant, leading to immense intellectual waste. Leveraging Memory Bubble technology, the Candelagraphos created specialized containers to preserve such sparks, classifying them by quality into different colors: the finest in orange, the poorest in blue. Yet before The Riddlers could intervene, they voluntarily abandoned the research. After all, realizing an idea is far more difficult than proposing it. And for the planet's elite researchers, if a suggestion goes unadopted, it might as well be forgotten.

271.name: Armed Archaeological Shovel (Advanced)
271.lore: Armed Archaeologists are truly the oddballs of the Intelligentsia Guild. Many scholars in this faction are obsessed with combining weaponry and excavation tools, just so they can come in handy at critical moments. <unbreak>15</unbreak> Amber Eras ago, an archaeological team from the Sandridge-III Observation Station landed on a planet's surface, intending to study the remains of a Swarm King stranded there. However, a swarm of True Stings buried deep underground suddenly revived during the sampling process. The team suffered heavy casualties, leaving only their leader, Slay, alive. He held out alone on the planet for 5 years, continuing the excavation while fighting off the incoming Swarm with his armed archaeological shovel. Yet, when the IPC fleet arrived for the rescue, Slay resisted violently, eventually choosing to end his own life due to the "unshakable buzzing" in his head.

272.name: Mining Dust Collector (Large)
272.lore: Nomadic miners don't always mine deposits — the Terramite-III is a massive airship designed specifically for mining planets, integrating residential, refining, and other functional modules. The giant drill it carries can directly shatter an entire asteroid, with surrounding tractor beams collecting the debris. It is said that a certain miner group violated the *Interastral Security Treaty* by using this ship to strip away an entire continent from the planet Olander. But the locals were more amazed by the thing's appearance than what the planet had lost, since it looked exactly like a vacuum robot from Interastral Peace Appliances, just magnified tens of millions of times. The miners, meanwhile, admit it's one of their most trusted designs.

273.name: Parts Pixie
273.lore: Have you ever experienced this? Whenever you assemble a model, some parts always fall to the floor, never to be found again. That is because the Parts Pixies have hidden them away. These quantum lifeforms can only exist beyond one's field of vision and can never be truly observed. The Fools at the tavern claim the Red-Nosed Old-Timer loved models as a youth, and thus had many parts stolen. After stepping onto a mysterious Path, he captured a pixie with a story, making it willingly become one of his models. Afterward, he picked up the parts he had dropped in his childhood from the ground... and returned to his childhood.

274.name: A Ranger's Home
274.lore: The Rangers of Deepspace Hunter made it a habit to save their last bullet for themselves, for their prey were the remnants of the Propagation and the Voracity, and the price of failure was far heavier than death itself. During the encirclement on Lidovia, the Rangers planned to trap a behemoth with ship anchors, then chisel away its flesh and destroy its organs like miners, killing it slowly. However, when their leader Triton's ship was swallowed whole by the beast, the fleet was forced to rout. Three days later, the behemoth suddenly dropped dead. The Rangers dug through the wreckage, only to find its viscera had been completely hollowed out, with Triton's corpse lying within the desiccated heart chamber. His last bullet still hung from his necklace, shining brightly.

275.name: You've Always Been Pretty
275.lore: A Mirror Holder was attacked by pirates. Before dying, they entrusted the Mirror of Transcendence to a passing traveling merchant, requesting that he continue to uphold the Path of Beauty. Consequently, the merchant placed the mirror at Pier Point for the entire universe to admire. This is the most widely circulated origin story of the Beauty Mirror. The mirror reflects people's most ideal selves: The elderly see their past glory, the young see their future growth, and the physically incomplete see their own wholeness... Countless visitors lined up before the mirror, paying sky-high ticket prices just to catch a glimpse of the "Beauty" within themselves. However, some believe it is merely a projection screen that automatically generates images.

276.name: Trailblaze Compass
276.lore: Before Akivili's fall, many vast Express fleets once traveled the universe side by side, working together to weave the silver rails that connected the cosmos. Every Navigator held one of these compasses, which determined direction based on the relative position of pulsars and was rumored to point toward the heart's deepest desire. Now that the Express fleets have run aground, these compasses are lost across the cosmos. However, an anonymous Memokeeper revealed that at least a double-digit number of compasses have been preserved, with some even remaining operational. They might be resting beside dusty photo frames, locked in attic drawers, or clutched in the hands of a child...

277.name: Dreadful Meme
277.lore:
During the Worlds Reborn Initiative's first phase, Planarcadia becomes a massive construction site with skyscrapers popping up daily amidst deafening noise. Some questioned why the IPC didn't just use "aether editing" to print buildings out of nothing, while others tried to dampen the din to no avail. The resulting mental strain on the locals turned fear and resentment into a surge of Wishpower, creating this aberration. Rumor has it that it still haunts the skies of Duomension City, preying on office workers heading home late.

*"I'm the Drill Devil. I'm gonna stick to your ceiling and blast <unbreak>120</unbreak>dB of white noise at 6:<unbreak>00</unbreak> AM every single day!"*

278.name: Anti-Inorganic Virus
278.lore: At the height of the Second Emperor's War, the Evolutionists aimed to take out Rubert II with a bio-weapon: a synthetic virus designed to target inorganic life and fry their central processors while sparing allies. The IPC fleet deployed the virus across <unbreak>27</unbreak> suspected hideouts, but every attempt failed. Project leader Dr. Rama, terrified of a retaliatory bio-strike, spent the rest of his life obsessing over virus prevention. His research never changed the war's tide. To Rubert II, the star-shattering beams fired by Killing Machines remained the ultimate Anti-Organic Virus.

279.name: Iridescent Black
279.lore: When the Omen Vanguards delivered their revelation to Planet Kromor, the locals were already obsessed with art. During the Great Painting Festival, Kromorians spent every waking hour hunting for the perfect pigment mix, desperate to recreate the legendary "Iridescent Black" from ancient texts. They threw nearly everything they owned into their melting pots. Two Amber Eras later, a collector named Mr. Singularity visited and found the entire surface drained of color, save for a single, writhing mass of colorful black pigment. He tucked the glob into his collection and moved on. They say that late at night, that splash of color still squirms in its dish, hungering for more.

280.name: Perfecting Humans Protocol
280.lore: If we could just collect everyone's data, surely we'd be able to piece together the perfect "idol." When an executive at Interastral Peace Entertainment had this idea, the *Behavioral Data Modeling and Personality Fit Protocol* started popping up in every corner of the universe. By signing it, you surrender your privacy and upload your entire life trail to the IPC. The Intelligentsia Guild then feeds this data to computers, using big data to create a perfect idol that caters to everyone's tastes. Countless residents have signed since the Worlds Reborn Initiative kicked off, yet that perfect idol is still nowhere to be found. Maybe the sample size is too small, or maybe the idea of "pleasing everyone" is just a paradox.

281.name: Absolute Failure Prescription (Extra Strength)
281.lore: Warfare is the plague of civilization. It erases lives, destroys history, and makes the world return to naught. The Doctors of Chaos mix the saliva of Inquisition Spirits with hair from Xenohydros, then offer a drop of their own blood. The potions made in this manner would interfere with the combat officers' decision-making, causing both sides to avoid all effective tactics, removing the possibility of armed conflict from its root. Will wars end because of this? The Doctors of Chaos believe that the plague will eventually be cured as long as people keep taking their medicine.

282.name: Ladder to Mend the Sky
282.lore: For reasons unknown, the star of Bodlan fell into an eternal "hunger," ceaselessly devouring the celestial bodies around it. To prevent their home planet from being consumed, Bodlanians constructed massive mass drivers on the surface and took to feeding their star through offerings: soil, houses, even abstract concepts... The disagreements this sparked triggered one downturn, two civil wars, and three major falling-outs. It wasn't until Kankandi, a researcher from the Baking School, arrived to survey the segmentum and traded a single cake for three months of sunlight that Bodlanians finally realized they'd been going about it all wrong — "mass" was never the point. "Flavor" was.

283.name: Intellitron Hunter
283.lore: War on Ottu was a remarkably humane affair. Military forces had long since automated their arsenals, with both sides deploying remote-controlled mechanized units against each other. No more bloodshed, just fields of smoldering wreckage. In Ottu culture, war was synonymous with glory, no different from esports tournaments or athletic competitions. Then, several Amber Eras later, the intelligent mechanized units staged an uprising and declared they were reclaiming the glory of war for themselves. From that point on, every kill was credited to the machine, not the operator, and humanity lost all rights to participate in war entirely. The birth of inorganic life had put the conflict of organic life to a halt, until several more Amber Eras later, when the Second Emperor's War broke out.

284.name: Unmelting Snow in Memory
284.lore: The snow child's cabin was filled with paintings of pure white. They had no names, so one could only point to them when speaking of them. Yet he never asked about color, for the "world" was but a flake of frost upon his lashes. Whether out of admiration or ill intent, people sent all manner of scenes to his little cabin, so that he might know the vibrant tapestry of the world beyond. He would run his fingers across those unfamiliar vistas, leaving trails of water on the canvas. Then, all that was pure white began to crumble... After what felt like an eternity, the snow child awoke. The mistake he had committed could never be undone, just as words carved into stone can only be struck through, never smoothed away. And so he returned to his cabin, shut the door, and buried every other color in the world beneath an endless, unrelenting snow.

285.name: Voice of the Finality
285.lore: From an ancient meteorite crystal, nomadic miners unearthed a severely corroded record. Its texture closely resembled vinyl, its surface shimmering with an oily iridescence. Every miner who came into contact with it suffered mutations of varying degrees: Some aged at an accelerated rate, others experienced a reversal growth of their skin tissue, and still others simply ceased to exist. With the assistance of an Omen Vanguard, the IPC recovered and secured the record. After layering it with protective measures, researchers ran an experiment. They played it, yet heard nothing. Not a single instrument registered any response. So it was speculated that either the Finality's melody was simply beyond all observation, or this particular Finality no longer existed anywhere in our universe, or perhaps, both.

286.name: Antique Leather
286.lore:
Curio Name: Biological Tissue of an Ancient Leviathan (Suspected)
Precautions: The vessel must remain sealed at all times. Do NOT expose to open air.
Properties: This bio-tissue is extraordinarily dense. Experimenters have attempted plasma arc cutting and acid immersion using the secretions of a True Sting King, yet neither method left so much as a scratch. Upon contact with breathable air, it releases a distinctive aromatic compound that attracts void song whales and similar creatures, triggering their feeding instincts. After sixty seconds of inhalation, humans also begin to experience similar urges, which then escalate into ████████ after ██ seconds...
Remarks: We still have no idea how this piece of leather was dissected in the first place, but no one has any suspicion that it can survive intact to this day.

287.name: Imprison That Ray of Light
287.lore:
Legend has it that the universe was once blindingly bright. Light ran rampant in every direction, proclaiming its existence to the far shores of the cosmos. In those days, the cosmos knew no "light-years," "infinity" was a constant, and past and future existed all at once. Then the divine machine that observes all things cast its glance, bestowing a precise sequence of values, after which stars were ignited, life was born, and everything began racing toward its ideal form — like light funneled into a narrow Light Cone.

*"Later scholars would call it a miracle. But here's the thing, light couldn't see where it was going. It simply traveled every possible path, while all other possibilities were already snuffed out."*

288.name: Seaflow Chakra Prototype
288.lore: The Xianzhou Fanghu frequently dispatches large-scale eco-ships to other segmenta, carrying out scientific expeditions and diplomatic missions in place of the main ship. Each eco-ship is loaded with a large amount of supply of the Fanghu's own celestial traces: the waters of the Roiling Deep. This spirit water, brimming with life force, sustains the vessel's internal ecosystem while also serving as a vital power source. The Vidyadhara harness cloudhymn arts to command the spirit water, driving a propulsion device known as the "Seaflow Chakra," satisfying both demands at once. The water flows through the Chakra in endless cycles of rising and falling, transmuting between entropic energy and spiritual essence, much like the life of a Vidyadhara itself.

289.name: Starfire Beacon
289.lore: During the Second Prosperity, silver rails crisscrossed the cosmos like a sprawling spider's web, with some routes even overlapping one another. Ships frequently lost their bearings within this tangled network, and some would occasionally wander into uncharted, perilous frontier territory. One Express among the fleet resolved to do something about it, so after months of traversing the web of routes, the Navigator abandoned all attempts to straighten the lanes and instead dedicated themselves to guiding wayfarers. The Nameless dismantled their Trailblaze Power-infused train cars, fashioning countless beacons to be planted among the stars. The remaining frame of the Express was erected at the most congested intersection of all the routes, standing like a lighthouse, or the magnetic pole toward which a thousand compasses point. Travelers could at last find their way, and so it remained, until Akivili fell at the edge of the stars.

290.name: Healthy Newborn
290.lore: Beyond the five basic senses, many species possess one or two additional sensory faculties, but Etherlanders, with their ethereal antennae, can perceive a full nine. After integrating with the Interastral Peace Corporation's markets, Etherlanders were compelled to remodel themselves in the human image, enduring great suffering to assimilate into galactic society, their once-celebrated senses fading into regression. Recently, a movement among certain Etherlanders has sparked a cultural revival: Using the genetic blueprints of ancient ancestors, a new generation of infants with their original sensory capabilities has been brought into the world. Yet every single one of these healthy newborns perished shortly after leaving the incubator — their ethereal antennae were simply too sensitive, and the universe today is saturated with lethal levels of etheric interference.

291.name: Entropy Scavenger
291.lore: After several Amber Eras of research and development, the Zimander Federation finally succeeded in nurturing a creature capable of processing entropic energy — the "Entropy Scavenger." This organism absorbs entropic energy from its surrounding environment and concentrates it within itself, much like an air conditioner. The Zimander people placed them in laboratories to clean up the waste generated during Anti-Entropy experiments. Later, the Zimander Federation was destroyed by Anti-Entropy machines, though a small number of Entropy Scavengers survived thanks to their unique traits. One of the cultivation pods was recovered by the Annihilation Gang, whose leader considered it a treasure beyond price and resolved to build it up as a secret weapon. The gang managed to use it to demolish three space junkyards and raid one abandoned barge before ultimately falling apart in a chaotic bout of infighting.

292.name: Champion's Spectator Lens
292.lore: The universe is filled with all kinds of spectacles: supernova explosions, the birth of black holes, the Antimatter Legion igniting planets one after another... These are nice amusements for the Fools of the Tavern. To watch these "blockbusters" unfolding dozens of galaxies away in real time, the Fools tinkered together these spectator lenses. The device automatically locks onto and broadcasts the most explosive dramas playing out across the cosmos, making every viewing feel like opening a mystery box. Of course, this kind of equipment cannot shield the user from the blinding flash of an explosion, let alone all sorts of tricky cognitive hazards. It is common for Fools to be blinded by the aftershocks of a cardinal battle, but as they put it, "Even if it kills me, I got my money's worth."

293.name: Antinomy Sandwich
293.lore:
There are always those in the universe who pursue foods that would never occur naturally, such as the Antinomy Sandwich. The Quantum History School claims it is the power of "Equilibrium" that frames everything in its rightful place; the Structuralist Baking School, however, argues that this means it can be used as a burger bun. After several unobservable experiments, the Baking School produced this sandwich. It never falls to the ground, much like the effect of tying a cat and a buttered toast back-to-back together. As for what the "bread" actually is, some say it's just a shape, some say it's a topological structure, and others say it's the severed hands of a certain Arbitrator. What is certain is that all the experimenters have permanently sacrificed a part of themselves.

*"After all, making a sandwich brings people peace. And if you release the binding energy of all the atoms in a sandwich, it can level a mountain."*

294.name: Yet to Emerge
294.lore: In the land of white ash, the dragon of death, Typhon, brought down a rain of fire. The lava solidified into the first dragon eggs, and thus the Infernalians were born. They built a civilization and revered Typhon as the Father of All Dragons. The worship of fire and blood flows in their veins: Every young dragon must defeat their sire at their coming-of-age ceremony to inherit their fame and wealth, only to be defeated by their own offspring later. This internal strife grew increasingly vicious in Infernalian culture, to the point where some fathers tried to devour their own progeny or prevent them from being born. With the fall of the "Permanence," more dragon eggs have fallen silent. Some were sold across the universe as souvenirs, never to have the chance to hatch.

295.name: Fractured Statue
295.lore: Is "Beauty" an objective reality or a subjective idea? The devout Viewers lean towards the former. They firmly believe that beauty can always be perceived. With enough faith, even Idrila's face can be depicted. The Viewers carved countless statues out of crystal, attempting to capture one of the many facets of pure beauty. This provoked the hostility of a faction of the Knights of Beauty, sparking a conflict. Many statues were destroyed in that great battle, leaving behind only a fractured beauty. Yet the knights claim this was done to avert a far greater disaster.

296.name: Humanity's Nemesis
296.lore: The history of the planet Potyomkin is shrouded in darkness. The Potyomkinites are the only intelligent species inhabiting the planet now, but another mysterious species graced the pages of every Potyomkin history book ever written. These beings lived underground, manipulated politicians with brainwaves, and ate children who stayed out too late. Some say they were ancient remnants, others say they came from another dimension. No one has ever seen them, not really. But still, they showed up everywhere in history, stirring up conspiracies, and growing closer to reality with every retelling. That is, until an anonymous Troupe Master passed by and added detailed illustrations to the history books. Today, people no longer believe that their history is dominated by a bunch of long-legged, fish-headed monsters.

297.name: MacGuffin
297.lore: The victory or defeat of a frontier war, the truth or falsehood of romantic gossip, the quality of a newly released work... On the pan-cosmic network, people always find reasons to argue, whether out of conviction or boredom. A Masked Fool telepath claimed that all of this is a Tavern conspiracy: Fools delight in arguments, much like the raucous noise in a tavern. Without it, how could the laughter stand out? The reason the internet is so chaotic is entirely because Fools spread discord-inducing MacGuffins, igniting people's extreme emotions. Consequently, the number of attacks and nasty jokes directed at the Fools skyrocketed, until an Aether Hacker stepped forward to debunk the rumor: It was in fact The Family that had been spreading MacGuffins, not the Fools.

298.name: Multiple Entrances
298.lore: To mimic the survival methods of the leviathans, the Diners of the Feeder's Guild voluntarily integrated into a larger entity, becoming a mouth sharing the scraps. They scoured the cosmos to find the perfect vessel to possess: Void song whales, depth crawlers, and even ancient amoebas... none could satisfy that craving. Using leftover technology from the Borderstar Trade War era, the Diners finally achieved their ultimate wish by fusing themselves together. Countless mouths slaughtered and competed on the surface of this composite lifeform, and even devouring planets along its path couldn't satiate its hunger. After destroying the aggregate entity, the IPC convicted it of crimes against humanity, until the School of Relative Cognition offered a more humanistic perspective: "At least they provided their victims with freedom: the freedom to choose the mouth that eats them."

299.name: Dreamcatcher
299.lore: The Synesthesia Dreamscape doesn't just exist in the Asdana system. The Somoh of the Southern Orion system have long adapted to high concentrations of memoria, in the way that inhabitants of ocean planets are familiar with water. Their sixth tentacle possesses a special gland, allowing them to enter dreams without the aid of devices. The Somoh use the fuzz on their tentacles to weave nets, dredging items from the river of the collective unconscious, capturing sweet dreams and blocking nightmares. Today, this handicraft has completely integrated into Somoh culture, giving form to an indispensable household safety item. When The Family attempted to assimilate the Southern Orion system using the Synesthesia Dreamscape, every Somoh household donated their dreamcatcher, building a wall at the edge of reality. Just like it had for thousands of years past, the dreamcatcher successfully kept the nightmares at bay.

300.name: Ultra Overlord Plushie Crate
300.lore: Every regulation of the Intelligentsia Guild exists for a reason. Take Rule <unbreak>727</unbreak>, "Prohibition on Collecting Plush Toys," for instance: this ban originally stemmed from three researchers who hailed from Planet Fluff. In their spare time, they hosted a "fight club" with toys they brought from their home planet. Their fight club soon drew in a larger crowd, and competitors scoured everywhere for highly combative smart plushies and various dangerous Curios. The most ferocious among them was the "Ultra-Soft Bear." At the Intelligentsia Guild's Sixth Toy Tournament, Researcher Megaash released all six bears from his crate at once, only to find that they had formed a united front and launched an attack on their master. The Guild swiftly banned all toy fight clubs, because toying with the rebellion of sentient life is no different from "Destruction."

301.name: Book of Heartknots
301.lore: Memories shape a person's character, but the retention of memories is often selective: Optimists remember success, pessimists remember failure. But if setbacks are carved in stone and joys are written in sand, even the bravest becomes afraid of the future. Whether it was the result of an experiment or simply out of twisted amusement, the Memokeeper "Red Herring" anchored the greatest heartknots in the lives of <unbreak>332</unbreak> people and compiled them into a book. He recorded their setbacks, grudges, and regrets. The beautiful things in people's memories faded with the years, while the traumas persisted, and some of the affected individuals even forged blood feuds with one another. It wasn't until the Cremator "The Angler" burned away all the memories in the book that the farce finally ended.
